description: I am a solo participant by history and by choice. Last year, after not being accepted into any team, I decided to face the hackathon entirely on my own. I am here to prove that a single human mind, augmented by artificial intelligence, can redefine how we communicate the future of space exploration.
summary:
What if a future intelligence discovered the technological remains left behind by humanity on other worlds and tried to reconstruct our story?

AFTER THE LAST LIGHT is an interactive storytelling experience inspired by NASA's Opportunity rover. It connects the story of Sophie Collis, the young student who named the rover, its extraordinary scientific legacy on Mars, and journalist Jacob Margolis's poetic interpretation of its final silence.

Through five narrative chapters, a curated NASA Evidence Archive, real mission images, scientific observations, engineering records, and documented references, the project introduces Sophia, a fictional future intelligence reconstructing humanity's exploration through surviving records.

Historical facts, human interpretations, poetry, philosophical reflections, and fiction are carefully distinguished and documented. By combining NASA resources, science communication, and creative storytelling, the experience invites audiences to explore Mars and reflect on what our machines may tell future intelligences about us.

Designed to reach audiences beyond the competition, the project has its own public domain, afterthelastlight.org, and is fully available in English and Brazilian Portuguese, connecting Brazilian audiences with a global community of learners and space enthusiasts.
details:
AFTER THE LAST LIGHT — The Memory of Opportunity is an interactive educational storytelling experience inspired by NASA's Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity and created in response to the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

The project explores a central question: if humanity's machines survive the civilizations that created them, what stories will they tell about us?


The experience introduces Sophia, a fictional future intelligence that attempts to reconstruct humanity's exploration of Mars through surviving technological records. Through five interactive narrative chapters, visitors follow Opportunity's story, from its naming and scientific achievements to the global dust storm that ended its mission and the technological legacy represented by autonomous systems such as AEGIS.


The project includes a curated NASA Evidence Archive, organized into five sections: Mission Records, Visual Evidence, Scientific Data, Engineering Archive, and Sources & Provenance. It brings together NASA mission information, real images, scientific observations, engineering records, and documented references in an accessible educational experience.


The experience distinguishes historical facts and scientific evidence from human interpretations, poetry, philosophical reflections, and fictional storytelling. It also contextualizes the popular phrase "My battery is low and it's getting dark," explaining that it was a journalist's poetic interpretation, not a literal transmission from the rover.


The project aims to make planetary exploration more accessible, encourage scientific curiosity, introduce audiences to the history and engineering of Mars exploration, and inspire reflection on technology, memory, and humanity's relationship with its machines.


The website is available in English and Brazilian Portuguese and combines interactive web-based storytelling, documentary research, visual communication, and audiovisual content. Its five chapters and documentary archive are designed to work together as an educational experience for a global audience.


Project website: https://afterthelastlight.org/
